properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-01: what flo2's Clerk and a team's Keycloak accept from a command-line OAuth client, and how far rmcp's `auth` feature already goes
properties.source: clerk.flo2.io's authorization-server metadata and api.flo2.io's 401, fetched 2026-10-01; Clerk and Keycloak 26.8.0 docs; draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-02; rmcp 3.4.0 src/transport/auth.rs
properties.statement:
flo2.io's AUTHORIZATION SERVER (Clerk, https://clerk.flo2.io), from its metadata fetched 2026-10-01:
- client_id_metadata_document_supported: true; code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]; authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true.
- No registration_endpoint, so DCR is off.
- Scopes include design:read, design:write and offline_access.
- It advertises a device_authorization_endpoint.
- No dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, so it offers no sender-constrained tokens.
- Clerk's docs for a CIMD client: public, PKCE S256 required, consent screen always shown, offline_access always included. The redirect URI "must exactly match an entry in redirect_uris".
- UNVERIFIED: whether a port-less loopback entry accepts any port. The indirect evidence says yes: Claude Code's CIMD lists http://localhost/callback and http://127.0.0.1/callback with no port and signs in to api.flo2.io.
- UNVERIFIED: whether Clerk rotates refresh tokens.

api.flo2.io's 401: Bearer resource_metadata=".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/g/<id>/mcp", scope="design:read design:write". The resource is PER DESIGN, https://api.flo2.io/g/<id>/mcp.

A TEAM'S KEYCLOAK (26.8.0): CIMD is experimental (--features=cimd plus a client policy), and resource indicators are experimental too. A typical team server will not have CIMD on, so a CLI needs a PRE-REGISTERED public client_id there. MCP says clients SHOULD offer static client credentials.

rmcp 3.4.0 `auth` (Apache-2.0, the official SDK). It already does:
- RFC 9728 discovery from the challenge or the well-known URIs, validating `resource`;
- RFC 8414 then OIDC discovery with the issuer check;
- registration in the order pre-registered, CIMD, DCR;
- PKCE S256, `resource` on authorize, token and refresh, and the RFC 9207 iss checks;
- union step-up with attempt limits, and a CredentialStore trait.

It does NOT run a loopback listener or open the browser. It only WARNS when code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, which MCP says to refuse. It falls back to legacy endpoints, which the resource-metadata MUST forbids. It pulls reqwest 0.13, oauth2 5 and url into a build that has no reqwest today. reflow2-mcp enables rmcp without `auth` (Cargo.toml:24).
